newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-"CROCODILE" DUNDEE A SNAPPY FINISHER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-"CROCODILE" DUNDEE A SNAPPY FINISHER.

text.p: When Berti Vogts called Sean Dundee into the German national squad on Tuesday it was another remarkable leap in a meteoric rise which has taken the South African-born player to the top of the Bundesliga scoring charts.

The snappy finisher -- nicknamed "Crocodile" by his team-mates -- began the 1995/96 season classed as an amateur with Karlsruhe, who signed him after spells with Stuttgart Kickers and regional league side Ditzingen.
Dundee, now 24, quickly established himself in the first team and had scored 16 league goals by the end of the season.
That tally put him second equal in the Bundesliga scorers' table, alongside such seasoned stars as Bayern Munich's Juergen Klinsmann and Giovane Elber of VfB Stuttgart.

But Dundee has not just made an impact on the field. The freckle-faced striker, who sports an earring, has also won friends for an amiable personality which seems increasingly rare in the big-business world of modern soccer.

"He's a dynamic young man, a great header of the ball and totally selfish. All strikers are totally selfish," Vogts said after announcing the squad. But he added: "I hope he keeps his carefree nature."
Dundee earned a call-up to the national squad of his native South Africa in December 1995 -- ironically the match was against Germany -- but withdrew because of injury.
Media reports suggested the "injury" was a convenient excuse for a player who had posters of Klinsmann and Thomas Haessler on his bedroom wall as a boy and dreamed of playing for Germany.

When it became clear Vogts was interested, Dundee, although of non-German origin, wasted no time in taking advantage of a special fast-track procedure for cases of "public interest" to apply for a German passport.

The issue became something of a political football, with South African politicians accusing Dundee of turning his back on his homeland while their German counterparts chimed in by asking why a soccer player should get special treatment.
Proof that Dundee has arrived in the big league of German sports stars was also in evidence as reports about his love life made the front page of the country's mass market press.

On the pitch, however, the unassuming striker's fortunes have gone from strength to strength. He was voted player of the year for 1996 by his fellow professionals and is the Bundesliga's leading scorer this season with 14 goals so far.
When the Interior Ministry announced in December that his application for German citizenship had been accepted, the news was a perfect early Christmas present.
